title: Portland Timbers to hire ex-Leicester manager Marti Cifuentes as next head coach: Sources
content:
The Portland Timbers are set to name Martí Cifuentes as their next head coach, sources briefed on the decision tell The Athletic.

Cifuentes, a 44-year-old Spaniard, will join the Timbers after the club parted ways with Phil Neville in May. Under interim manager Jack Cassidy, Portland returned from the World Cup break Thursday night with an emphatic 5-1 win over the rival Seattle Sounders and sit 11th in the Western Conference, three points below the playoff line with 19 matches left. Cifuentes is set to take the reins from Cassidy upon the receipt of his visa. The club’s next match is Wednesday night at home against FC Dallas.

The Timbers landed on Cifuentes for the permanent job based on his tactical acumen and attacking mentality, sources say. He is a young manager with plenty of experience, having coached Leicester City, QPR and Hammarby, among others.

Sources say the other finalists in the Timbers’ extensive coaching search were Panama head coach Thomas Christiansen and former Austin FC head coach Josh Wolff. As previously reported by The Athletic, the club also had talks with Jim Curtin, who was named Austin head coach in June but won’t start until the 2027 season.

Portland interviewed a wide number of candidates based both domestically and abroad, including ones that have since gotten jobs in Europe, sources add.

Cifuentes was most recently with Leicester City. The club surprisingly fired him in January when the team was in 14th, but six points off the playoff places. Leicester would go on to win just one of its next 15 matches and were relegated.

Before Leicester, Cifuentes spent a season and a half with QPR. He took over a team that was second-to-last in the 2023-24 campaign and guided them to safety. QPR finished 15th in his lone full season in charge.

The Timbers squad will evolve this summer, but the team believes a number of key players will fit well under Cifuentes, namely designated players Kristoffer Velde and David Da Costa.

Beyond that attacking duo, Venezuelan international forward Kevin Kelsy is the team’s leading scorer with seven goals, two of which came Thursday vs. Seattle. Center back Finn Surman just represented New Zealand at the World Cup, where he scored against Egypt. Cole Bassett, who also scored vs. the Sounders, was acquired in a key trade with the Colorado Rapids this winter.
